items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I don't believe it about Sidney Allen... [INTERVIEWEE] And I knew Brian Gilbert for a long time. I didn't really know him. What about the one-armed trumpet player?

ctx.x: They had circles that week. I'm going to tell you, the last parade I've prayed in my life. The last time I prayed. It was in 1919, they had a car strike. See? And we had to walk from the heritage, we were all human, you see? But we had to hide outside men. So, Shilling got a job. Around 1919. 18 or 19. Because they would have a meet at the old Crescent Theatre. You know the Crescent Theatre? You don't remember the Crescent Theatre? Tulane and Tulane. Tulane, Tulane, yeah. All right. So, Shilling says, come on. I…

Where did you live then, Johnny? Around the prime evening off? Oh, yeah. I lived the whole hallway around the street. You still live on Orleans? No, I don't live around that way anymore. But that was 1990. Bache used to live around that too, didn't he? Bache. Bache, he died, yeah. Yeah, Bache, yeah. I was, when I was, yeah, Sidney, yeah.

Yeah, Sidney Bache. I was working around 1910, 1911, 12. Sharky's brother-in-law, Johnny Carella, had all the camps. I was building, but Sharky was learning how to play. I used to leave him sitting on the bandstand, he was building all this. For Christ's sake, Johnny, I don't want that monkey to eat camp. I said, leave him playing.
